# `notifyd-client` rubygem

To make it easy for the monolith (and any other ruby project) to integrate with notifyd we have a Ruby gem. This is mainly a client wrapper for our Twirp APIs.

## Source

The source for the gem lives in the [`/ruby`](../ruby) directory in this repository. Some of the code is auto generated from the Twirp API definitions, and some is hand-written to make consuming the auto-generated code easier.

Together with the code we also publish RBI definitions for it, which allows [sorbet][sorbet] to gradually type check our Ruby code.

You can learn more about sorbet, how to use it and the options it has on [its website][sorbet].

### Generating sorbet files

After changing ruby code you might need to re-generate sorbet files both in `Notifyd` and `Dotcom` codebases.

**Notifyd**
After changing contents of `/ruby` folder run the following:

```
// Build brand new version of ruby image, use it for updating gems
make docker-build-test-ruby

// It will run checks for your existing files
make tapioca

// It will re-generate files with tapioca
make tapioca TAPIOCA_ARGS="dsl"
```

Please note, Sorbet setup ignores Twirp generated files on Notifyd side for now: https://github.com/github/notifyd/blob/main/ruby/sorbet/config

**Dotcom**

When `Dotcom` codebase consumes a new gem, `notifyd-client` in our case, we need to generate corresponding `rbi` files for it.
Process is described in this doc https://thehub.github.com/epd/engineering/products-and-services/dotcom/sorbet/

For notifyd case you might be interested in those 2 commands to regenerate rbi files:

```
./bin/tapioca dsl
./bin/tapioca gem  notifyd-client
```

## Adding twirp services/endpoints

1. When you have added the protobuf definitions for new twirp endpoints/services in [`/proto/services`](../proto/services), you can then run `make generate` to generate updated ruby client code.

   Once you've done this you should see new code in the [`/ruby/lib/notifyd/proto/services`](../ruby/lib/notifyd/proto/services) directory.

   Once the Ruby code is generated from the `proto` definitions we also need to make sure that the sorbet definitions are updated for them.

   ```sh
   make rbi TAPIOCA_ARGS=dsl
   ```

   If you have just added an endpoint to an existing service that's all you need to do.

   1. Make sure to update the version number in the [`ruby/lib/notifyd/version.rb`](../ruby/lib/notifyd/version.rb) file.
   1. Run bundler in the [`ruby`] directory to update the `Gemfile.lock` with any new dependencies.
2. If you've added a new service then you need to add the generated ruby code
   to the `ruby/sorbet/config` file as an ignore. Unfotunately the ruby files
   generated by `protoc` are not "typable" by sorbet, so we need to rely on RBI
   purely for this, in order for the RBIs to have precedence we need to tell
   sorbet they are the source of truth for those types by ignoring the ruby
   files. As an example, for the new maintenance service we had to add this
   line:

   ```
    --ignore=lib/notifyd/proto/services/maintenance/service_pb.rb
   ```

## Versioning

There are several different _versions_ within notifyd:
- The [Ruby client version](../ruby/lib/notifyd/version.rb).
- The [Monolith Twirp version](../proto/monolith-twirp/notifyd/VERSION).
- The [notifyd repository tags](https://github.com/github/notifyd/tags).

These versions should be kept consistent. In order to do this, whenever there's a change to either the notifyd or monolith APIs, bump the minor version in both version files.
Once the changes are merged, push a new corresponding tag.

## Updating the gem in the monolith

We don't "publish" this gem anywhere yet. Instead it is built from source and directly vendored into `github/github`.

1. Update the version number in the `Gemfile` to the new version.
   ```gemfile
   gem "notifyd-client",      "1.9.1"
   ```
2. Execute the bundler to vendor the new version of the gem.
   ```sh
   bin/bundle install
   ```
3. Open a PR to deploy as normal.

To test changes that have not yet been merged to `main` you can temporarily build the gem from a different branch by specifying the ref. Don't forget to re-vendor the gem before opening a PR on `github/github`.

```gemfile
gem "notifyd-client",      "1.9.1", github: "github/notifyd", ref: "ac2eb4d99d25c3411e9c685fa21dd7d4c6d869bc"
```

[sorbet]: https://sorbet.org "Sorbet"
